To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the extracts of Bersama abyssincia Fresen., Combretum paniculate Vent., Dodonaea angusifolia L.f and Ximenia americane L. exhibited antiviral activity.

the extracts of Bersama abyssinic, Combretum panicualtum, Dodonaea angusitifolia, and Ximenia americans showed antiviral activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel antiviral agents from plants used in the traditional medical system in Ethiopia.
the identification and isolation of biologically active natural products from plants.
the identification and characterization of new compounds from Ethiopian plants with potential for the treatment of human immunodeficiency viral infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the present study, the antiviral activity of 71 extracts derived from 14 plant species belonging to 21 families, was evaluated against HIV-1 and HIV-2 strains.
the antiviral activity of these extracts is due to the synergistic effects of the compounds present in them.
the extracts from the plants tested showed some degree of antivirality against HIV‐1 and HIV‐2, but none of the extracts tested showed a high level of selectivity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the extracts of Combretum and Dodonaea species were active against both HIV‐1 and HIV‐2.
we were able to find 6 extracts that showed antiretrovirus activity and were not toxic to the cells.
the plant extracts from Combretum paniculate and Ximenia Americana were found to be active against HIV‐1 and HIV‐2, respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are many plants in the world that have the potential to be useful in treating HIV/AIDS.
we have found some plants that are active against HIV-1 and/or HIV-2.
the extracts from the plants tested in this work have a high potential to be developed as anti-HIV drugs.
